passage: Dear Tenzin, Thank you for meeting me twice and for being so patient while I took ten days to answer. My answer is no, and I want to give you the reasons rather than leave you guessing. I would like to finish my research posting in Pune, and you hope to move to Dharamshala soon; I do not want either of us to give up a plan we love. I said the same to my parents this week, calmly, and I will say it again if they ask again. I enjoyed our conversations and would be glad to stay in touch as friends, if you'd like that. I also know an old classmate who is hoping to meet someone, and I will introduce you only if you want me to. Warm wishes, Vinita

qa.q: How many days did Vinita take to answer?
qa.a: Vinita took ten days to answer.

qa.q: What is Vinita feeling while writing, and what shows it?
qa.a: Vinita feels calm, kind and firm. Vinita gives reasons, thanks Tenzin and repeats the no without harshness.

qa.q: Which choices in Vinita's letter made the refusal easier for Tenzin to hear?
qa.a: Vinita gave clear reasons, thanked Tenzin for the patience, offered friendship and an optional introduction, and blamed no one.

qa.q: How might Tenzin feel on reading the letter?
qa.a: Probably disappointed but respected, since Vinita took time, gave honest reasons and stayed warm.

grounding: A young adult declines a match with reasons, alternatives and a considered delay, and repeats the calm no to their own parents.

passage: So Jyoti Masi rang again about the match, the third time this month. I had already taken a week to think. This time I said, "Masi, thank you for caring enough to search. My answer is no. I want to finish my nursing course, and I don't feel anything for him." She said, "Just meet him once." I said, "I understand you want me settled. The answer is still no, but I'd love to visit you on Sunday." She tried again about the family being so good. I repeated it kindly, same words, no shouting. My hands were cold the whole call. At the end she sighed and said, "You sound like your mother." I couldn't tell if it was a compliment. But on Sunday she made my favourite kheer, and nobody mentioned the boy. Charu

qa.q: What did Charu want to finish?
qa.a: Charu wanted to finish the nursing course.

qa.q: What was Charu feeling during the call, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Charu felt nervous but stayed calm. Charu's hands were cold the whole call, yet the same kind answer was repeated without shouting.

qa.q: Which choice did Charu make on the call, and what did it achieve that a sudden fight might not?
qa.a: Charu repeated the same kind no. The kind, repeated no kept the bond with Jyoti Masi warm, as the Sunday visit and kheer show, while the answer never changed.

qa.q: How might Jyoti Masi have felt when Charu said no again?
qa.a: Probably disappointed and worried, since she sighed, but still caring, as the Sunday kheer shows.

grounding: A young adult who does not want a match says so with reasons, takes time, offers a visit instead, and repeats the calm no kindly.
